notes: §1985:VIII.3.2.4 GR3 makes the relative DATA RECORDS clause the sequential one, which 'serves only as documentation' (§1985:VII.3.5.1) with the format DATA { RECORD IS | RECORDS ARE } { data-name-1 } ... and SR1 'Data-name-1 is the name of a data record and must have an 01 level-number record description' (§1985:VII.3.5.3). dataRecordsClause parses it with IS/ARE optional, FileDescriptionFormats.Rows admits it in every FD format (deleted at 2002), BindFileSection calls ScreenDataRecords for SR1 (COBOL6849), the clause changes no I-O, and VisitDataRecordsClause refuses it from 2002 (COBOL0873). Probes at 85 on a relative file (random and dynamic) with a fixed and an OCCURS DEPENDING ON record: RECORDS ARE both names, RECORD IS one, RECORDS without ARE in either order, RECORD with two names, and beside LABEL RECORDS each compile and run unchanged (ABCDEFGHIJ / 3 3XYZ); (b) no data-name (COBOL0001), DATA RECORDS IS (syntax error), a WORKING-STORAGE item, a level-05 item, another file's 01 and an undefined name (COBOL6849) and the clause written twice (COBOL2423) are refused; a name listed twice is accepted, which no 1985 rule forbids; at --std 2002 the clause is COBOL0873. The witness names two 01 records (one group) and writes and reads both.

next.reason: 1985: "The DATA RECORDS clause is an obsolete element in Standard COBOL because it is to be deleted from the next revision"; 2023: "No DATA RECORDS clause: the 13.4.5.4 file description entry rules cover BLOCK CONTAINS, CODE-SET, LINAGE, RECORD, REPORT only". 1985 marks DATA RECORDS obsolete and due for deletion. The 2023 file description rules list other clauses but never DATA RECORDS, so the clause is dropped.
